## Round 2 diff-only security review (HEAD 53703f8b)

- Source: `<transcripts>/148019cc-de64-4bee-8c80-932a311792cc/subagents/agent-a07d11fdc6d851747.jsonl` (final assistant message)
- Timestamp: 2026-10-29T22:32:13.384Z

## Security Review Findings: round 2, diff `8d2b41ce..53703f8b`
Most of the round-1 fixes hold. I re-ran all 56 round-1 payloads against the hook at `53703f8b`. Every one asks except those the "Not covered" paragraph lists and the plain `git push origin main`, which is a branch push and is journaled. The named suite `tests/run.sh e2e-tier-gate.test.sh` passed 1300 checks with 0 failures, exit 0, at `53703f8b`.
block-unchecked-merge now blocks `g\h pr merge 1`, `gh p\r merge 1` and `gh pr mer\ge 1` (exit 2). The `=` form `--config-env=...=X`, `caffeinate git push --tags`, `GIT_CONFIG_*=… git push`, the GraphQL Ref/Release/Merge mutations (including a field and its `(` on separate lines), line continuations, and heredoc bodies piped to `sh` all ask.
### P1 — Critical Security Issues (Blocks Merge)
| **SEC-1 · security · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:711`**<br>`gh api -X=POST repos/o/r/releases -f tag_name=v9`, `-X=PATCH .../releases/1`, `-X=DELETE .../git/refs/tags/v1.0.0` and `-X=POST .../git/refs -f ref=refs/tags/v9` are all allowed with no output. gh accepts `-X=VALUE`, but the `-X?*` arm keeps `=POST` as the method. That fails the `POST\|PUT\|PATCH\|DELETE` check at line 760, and the whole call is dropped. Release creation, publishing and tag deletion have no other confirmation. The merge form (`-X=PUT .../pulls/1/merge`) is blocked only by block-unchecked-merge. _(HIGH)_ | In the `-X?*` arm, strip one leading `=` (`method="${t#-X}"; method="${method#=}"`). Then treat any method that is still not a known verb as unreadable, which asks, instead of returning 0. Add e2e cases for `-X=POST`, `-X=DELETE` and `-X=PUT`. |
### P2 — Security Concerns
| **SEC-2 · security · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:450`**<br>`git --config-env remote.origin.mirror=X push`, `--config-env remote.origin.push=X` and `--config-env push.followTags=X` (space form) are allowed. Git accepts the space form: the dry run listed both tags as `[new tag]`. Only `--config-env=*` (line 427) reads the key. The space form goes to the skip arm at 450, so the header's claim to cover "the same through --config-env" is true for only one spelling. _(HIGH)_ | Handle `--config-env` with a separate value the same way as `--config-env=`: read `TOK[j+1]` and apply the same key cases. |
| **SEC-3 · security · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:595`**<br>The push remote is taken only from `words[0]` or the repository's own config (line 624). `git push --repo=mir`, `--repo mir`, `git -c remote.pushDefault=mir push` and `git -c branch.main.pushRemote=mir push` are allowed when `mir` is a mirror remote. The dry run showed all tags pushed and the remote-only tag `v5` deleted. The header (lines 72-75) says a remote's mirror and push configuration count. `--repo` is skipped as a plain value, and `-c` is read only for followTags, mirror and push keys. _(HIGH)_ | When `--repo`/`--repo=` is given and there is no positional remote, use its value as the remote. Treat `-c` settings of `remote.pushDefault`, `branch.*.pushRemote` and `branch.*.remote` (and the same through `--config-env` or `GIT_CONFIG_*`) as cfg=1, which asks. |
| **SEC-4 · security · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:935`**<br>A command passed as one quoted argument to a program the hook does not know is not read. Allowed: `watch 'gh release create v9'`, `watch -n 30 'gh pr merge 1 --squash'`, `script -q /dev/null -c 'git push --tags'`, `flock /tmp/l -c 'gh release create v9'`, `tmux new -d '...'`, `trap 'gh release create v9' EXIT`. `_tg_scan` compares each word's basename with gh/git, and the single word `gh release create v9` never matches. The header (lines 179 and 921) names `watch` and `script -q /dev/null` as covered, but only the unquoted form is, and the quoted form is how `watch` is usually written. The merge forms here also pass block-unchecked-merge (exit 0). The same gap applies to `env -S'...'` and `env --split-string='...'`, which are allowed while `env -S '...'` asks (line 320 handles only the separate-value form). _(HIGH)_ | In `_tg_scan`, read any word that contains whitespace after an unknown program as a command: run it through the same tokenize-and-classify path and keep Tier 3 results. Handle the attached forms `-S…` and `--split-string=…` for env. Pin `watch '...'`, `flock -c`, `trap` and `env -S'…'` in the e2e suite. |
### P3 — Security Improvements
| **SEC-5 · security · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:662`**<br>A destination that is not a tag locally is treated as a branch even when the remote has that tag. `git push --force-with-lease=v5:<sha> origin HEAD:v5`, where `v5` is a tag only on the remote, moves the remote tag: the dry run showed `HEAD:refs/tags/v5 (forced update)`. Neither tier-gate nor block-force-push asks, because block-force-push allows `--force-with-lease`. `-f` and `+` are refused by block-force-push, and a bare `--force-with-lease` is rejected by git as stale. _(HIGH)_ | When the destination is not under `refs/` and is not a local branch either, treat it as unread (ask), matching the source rule and the deletion rule. |
| **SEC-6 · security · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:827`**<br>`gh api repos/o/r/git/refs -F ref=@ref.txt` is allowed. A ref value read from a file is not recognized as unreadable, unlike `--input`. _(MEDIUM)_ | Treat a `ref=@…` value (from `-F`) as unreadable, which gives tagUnread. |
| **SEC-7 · security · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:459`**<br>`git -c push.followTags=2 push` is allowed. Git reads any non-zero integer as true (`git -c push.followTags=2 config --type=bool --get push.followTags` prints `true`), but the `push.followtags=*` arm sets follow=0. _(HIGH)_ | Set follow=0 only for git's false spellings (false/no/off/0/empty). Anything else is follow=1, or unknown when it cannot be read. |
| **SEC-8 · security · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:187`**<br>The "Not covered" paragraph does not mention two allowed spellings: `export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=remote.origin.mirror GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=true; git push`, and a `cd` earlier in the same command that moves `git push` into a repository whose configuration has followTags or mirror (the lookups use the payload's directory). `git -c include.path=…` is also unlisted. These are close to the listed "GIT_DIR set by export" exclusion, but the paragraph should say so. _(MEDIUM)_ | Add them to the exclusions paragraph, or count GIT_CONFIG_* exports and `cd` for git the way TG_GHMOVED already does for gh. |
### Dependency Audit (separate from finding schema — no file:line)

## Round 2 diff-only code review (HEAD 53703f8b)

- Source: `<transcripts>/148019cc-de64-4bee-8c80-932a311792cc/subagents/agent-adac421c6b2bb0c6a.jsonl` (final assistant message)
- Timestamp: 2026-10-29T22:33:30.754Z

Everything below was checked against HEAD `53703f8b6e36773685fa450360ef1dc9acb5f1bc`, which did not move during the review. I fed JSON payloads to the hook in scratch repositories and compared results with the base `8d2b41ce`, extracted read-only. The named suite `tests/run.sh e2e-tier-gate.test.sh` passed at HEAD (pass=1300 fail=0, rc=0), even though F1 is present.
## Code Review Findings
### P1 — Critical (Blocks Merge)
| **F1 · correctness · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:610`**<br>`_tg_git_push` reads redirection words as remotes and refspecs: `*) words+=("$t")` keeps `2>&1`, `>/dev/null`, `2>/dev/null` and `> out.log`. This round added the rule "a source that is not a local branch asks" (`:666`), so those words now trigger a possible-tag-push prompt. Base let all of these through; HEAD asks for each: `git push origin my-branch 2>&1`, `git push -u origin my-branch 2>&1`, `git push origin my-branch >/dev/null`, `git push origin my-branch 2>/dev/null`, `git push origin my-branch > out.log 2>&1`, `git push -u origin HEAD 2>&1 \| tail -3`. The opposite failure also happens. In `git push 2>&1`, the `2>&1` becomes `words[0]`, so `:623` looks up the configuration of a remote literally named `2>&1`, and the new mirror check is skipped. In a repository with `remote.origin.mirror = true`, `git push` asks, but `git push 2>&1`, `git push >/dev/null` and `git push -q 2>&1 \| tail -2` pass without a prompt. `_bd_is_redirection` exists in lib/command-parse.sh and block-unchecked-merge.sh uses it, but tier-gate.sh never calls it. _(HIGH)_ | Skip redirection words, and the target word of a split `>`/`2>`, before `words+=` in `_tg_git_push`. Use `_bd_is_redirection`, as block-unchecked-merge.sh does. Apply the same filter to the positional loops in `_tg_release` and `_tg_api`. |
### P2 — Should Fix
| **F2 · tests · `plugins/flow/tests/e2e-tier-gate.test.sh:704`**<br>No scenario sends a push that has a redirection. The only `2>&1` near a push in the file is the harness's own setup at :704, not a payload. The suite passes 1300/0 with F1 present. _(HIGH)_ | Add must-pass cases (`git push -u origin HEAD 2>&1`, `git push origin <branch> >/dev/null` → journaled, not asked). Add a must-ask case: a mirror remote with `git push 2>&1`. |
| **F3 · correctness · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:420`**<br>A relative `GIT_DIR=` (new this round) is resolved against the payload's directory before the option loop sees `-C`. A `--git-dir=` written before `-C` is resolved the same way (`:447`, against `base` as it stands at that point). git resolves a relative git dir only after `-C`: `GIT_DIR=.git git -C ../other rev-parse --absolute-git-dir` prints `other/.git`. So with tag `rel` in `../other` and a branch `rel` in the payload repository, `GIT_DIR=.git git -C ../other push origin rel` and `git --git-dir=.git -C ../other push origin rel` pass as branch pushes. `git -C ../other push origin rel` correctly asks. This is a missed tag push in a path the round-1 fix added. _(HIGH)_ | Keep `gd`/`wt` as written while parsing the options, and make them absolute after the loop against the final `base`. |
### P3 — Consider
| **F6 · correctness · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:753`**<br>The GraphQL field scan also picks up names inside string literals, and `*ref*` matches ordinary words such as `prefer`, `refactor` and `reference`. Asked as a release: `addPullRequestReviewThreadReply(... body:"Fixed in abc (refactor(gate): split)")` and `updatePullRequest(... body:"prefer(x)")`. Asked as a merge: `addPullRequestReview(... "refactor(x) and merge(y)")`. `disablePullRequestAutoMerge`, which makes nothing merge, is also treated as a merge (`:755-757`). These only cost extra prompts; nothing is missed. A field name on one line with its `(` on the next is still caught. _(HIGH)_ | Remove `"..."` and `"""..."""` literals and `#` comments from the text before the `grep -oE`. Add `disablepullrequestautomerge` to the exempt list. |
| **F7 · performance · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/lib/command-parse.sh:140`**<br>`_bd_unescape` starts a `sed` process for every word over 64 characters that holds a backslash. It runs from both `_bd_unescape_tok` and `_bd_expand_interpreter_args` (`:567`), and in both hooks. A command of 300 such words took 1.05s against 0.16s with `_bd_unescape` stubbed out, and 2.12s against 0.24s behind `timeout`. Ordinary pushes went from about 0.18s to 0.21–0.35s because of the new remote and config lookups. _(HIGH)_ | Unescape all long words in one `sed`/`awk` call per simple command, or raise the substitution threshold. Measure again with both hooks. |
| **F8 · correctness · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:415`**<br>`GIT_CONFIG*=*` also matches `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, which cannot add a key. `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 git push origin my-branch` asks. _(HIGH)_ | Match `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_*`, `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`, `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` and `GIT_CONFIG` only. |

### Acceptance Criteria Verification
### Findings
#### P1 — Critical (Blocks Merge)
| **INT-1 · runtime · `plugins/flow/commands/release.md:633`**<br>The tier table and the paragraph after it name `flow.tiers.push`, `flow.tiers.prCreate` and `flow.tiers.release` (lines 633, 634, 640, all added on this branch). The hook reads top-level `tiers.*`. In `settings.json`, `tiers` is a top-level key and `.flow` only holds goals, runtime, triggers and workflows. Confirmed at runtime: with `{"flow":{"tiers":{"push":"confirm","prCreate":"confirm"}}}`, `git push` and `gh pr create` were journaled without asking. With `{"tiers":{…}}` both asked. So a user who follows this doc to require a prompt before push gets journal-only, and nothing says the setting was ignored. Searching the plugin, outside `evals/`, found no other `flow.tiers` in instructions; the tier-gate test header mentions it only as a known failure mode. _(HIGH)_ | Change the three mentions to `tiers.push`, `tiers.prCreate` and `tiers.release`, the names used in `references/three-tier-safety.md` and `commands/merge.md:866`. |
#### P2 — Should Fix
#### P3 — Consider
### Overall: FAIL
